author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing opens at the first page when asked for a page before the first
summary: An owner listing asked for a page before the first shows the first page of owners instead of an error page. The behavior holds whether or not a last name was searched for.
acceptance_criteria: given an owner listing asked for a page before the first, when it runs, then the first page of owners is listed
given that same request, when the reply is checked, then it is the ordinary listing rather than an error page
given a last-name search asked for a page before the first, when it runs, then it behaves as the first page of that search's results
non_goals: behavior for a page after the last page of results
behavior for a page value that is not a number
notes: Grounded in the intake-decision at handoff.jsonl line 1; the owner recorded no decisions beyond the request as stated. The request names only page values below the first, so the two non_goals above are undecided and out of this slice, not declined scope — neither is a Non-Goals table row and the PRD's Non-Goals table is unchanged. PRD: docs/prd.md, Owner records, REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001 with edge case 4.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Existing pattern with a one-line adjustment at the same boundary. Cause located by reading OwnerController.java: processFindForm binds page with @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1"), and findPaginatedForOwnersLastName calls PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize). Any page below 1 makes that argument negative, PageRequest.of throws IllegalArgumentException, and the unhandled exception renders the error page. The fix is request normalization in the controller, which the Web controller row of architecture-principles.md admits as binding work rather than a business rule. The same method already normalizes the other bound parameter (lastName null becomes empty, otherwise stripped), so the page clamp is that precedent applied to the second parameter. security-principles.md Trust Boundaries places this check at the arrival point of external input, which is where it belongs. Basis: grep and full read of OwnerController.java and OwnerControllerTests.java, no IDE oracle connected on this dispatch, so the resolution is the weaker text-based basis.
integration_points: processFindForm is the single entry for both the parameterless listing and the last-name search, so normalizing there satisfies all three acceptance criteria through one change
addPaginationModel publishes currentPage to owners/ownersList.html, whose pager builds first/previous/next/last links from it

patterns.description: existing normalization of a bound request parameter inside processFindForm: lastName null becomes empty string, otherwise stripped. Normalize page the same way, in the same method
existing MockMvc paging test shape: stub findByLastNameStartingWith with a PageImpl, perform the GET, assert status and view name

risks.risk: Normalizing only inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName leaves the raw value flowing to addPaginationModel, so currentPage reaches the view as 0 or negative and the pager renders wrong links while the status is 200
risks.mitigation: Normalize once at the top of processFindForm and pass the normalized value to both the query helper and addPaginationModel. Cover it with a model attribute assertion on currentPage, not status alone

risks.risk: A test that asserts only status 200 and the view name passes even if the wrong page of results is fetched
risks.mitigation: Capture the Pageable reaching findByLastNameStartingWith and assert its page index is 0, alongside the status and view assertions

risks.risk: VetController.findPaginated carries the identical unguarded page - 1 arithmetic, so /vets.html?page=0 still renders the error page after this slice lands
risks.mitigation: Out of scope here: the prd-entry and REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001 name owners only. Leave the vet route untouched and let a separate slice decide it, rather than widening this one

notes: No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. Five-signal foundational check: none tripped. system-design.md is confirmed and populated, ADRs record the language, framework and architecture shape, ubiquitous-language.md is written and confirmed, the web boundary has a recorded pattern, and no new bounded context appears. One durable-memory write accompanied this triage: docs/system-design.md Contracts table, OwnerController row now cites REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001 and names the parameter normalization. No ADR: clamping a bound request parameter is a straightforward implementation choice with no trade-off to record. No Known Defects row was added for the current behavior, since this slice removes it. Reviewer note: the clamp is request binding, not a fresh business rule in a controller, so the architecture-principles.md open deviation is not extended by it.

addPaginationModel and findPaginatedForOwnersLastName correctly receive the clamped requestedPage, keeping model state and query state consistent

docs/prd.md and docs/system-design.md updated consistently with the code change (requirement id, contract description, edge case)

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply-chain check not run: this project configures no OWASP dependency-check plugin (build.gradle has java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management 1.1.7, graalvm native 1.1.2, cyclonedx-bom 3.2.4, javaformat 0.0.47), and the reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match was performed in this review. Resolved framework baseline is Spring Boot 4.1.0. The diff adds no dependencies, so this is unchanged-baseline reporting, not a regression — a human or CI should close it against the NVD. The cyclonedx SBOM task is the natural hook.

Pattern divergence, pre-existing and therefore not a finding under security-principles.md ('pre-existing absences in that baseline are never findings'): VetController.showVetList (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/VetController.java:45) takes the identical `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page` and passes it unclamped to PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) at line 61, so /vets.html?page=0 still renders the error page and page=Integer.MIN_VALUE still underflows into a huge-OFFSET query. After this slice the two paging endpoints normalize the same concern differently. Worth a follow-up slice so the codebase has one way to normalize a page parameter.
approved_aspects: Boundary validation: the request-derived `page` is normalized at the controller boundary (OwnerController.java:113) before it reaches PageRequest.of, matching security-principles.md 'Validate type, range, and shape before use'.

Removes an integer-underflow path: page=Integer.MIN_VALUE previously reached `page - 1` and wrapped to Integer.MAX_VALUE, producing a ~10.7-billion-row OFFSET query; Math.max clamps it to 1 first. The change is strictly stronger than the baseline here.

Fail-secure error handling improved: a page below 1 no longer raises IllegalArgumentException into the 500 error page, which renders exception text (security-principles.md secret-disclosure row); one fewer request-controlled exception message reaches a rendered page.
No injection surface added: lastName still flows through the Spring Data derived query `findByLastNameStartingWith` (parameterized), and no query text is concatenated.

No new output surface: `currentPage` remains a primitive int, so the pre-existing Thymeleaf preprocessing in ownersList.html (`__${currentPage - 1}__`, lines 44/49/54) cannot carry request-supplied SpEL text; binding rejects non-numeric input before the model is populated.
Mass-assignment control untouched: the @InitBinder disallow list for `id`/`*.id` is intact, and no new request-bound type was introduced.
No credentials, secrets, logging, file I/O, shell execution, deserialization, or reflection introduced; grep over the diff for Runtime/ProcessBuilder/Files./JsonTypeInfo//tmp/ returned nothing.
Resource bounds unchanged: page size stays fixed at 5, so no request-controlled allocation.
No dependency or build change: build.gradle is outside the change set, so the supply-chain surface is identical to the reviewed baseline.
Test additions are read-only MockMvc drives with no security-relevant surface of their own.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owner listing page parameter to the first page

blast_radius.note: One module and four files: eleven added lines in OwnerController, seventy-four test lines, and two doc rows. No sensitive paths, no dependency or build change, and the clamp is confined to processFindForm, whose two callees already took a page number.

semantic_surprise.note: I read every hunk. Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) does exactly what its name and comment say for every int: zero and negatives become one, Integer.MIN_VALUE becomes one rather than wrapping through the decrement, and any page of one or more is untouched, so paging past the first page is unchanged. The clamped value reaches both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, so currentPage in the view can no longer disagree with the page actually fetched, and the empty-result and single-result branches are byte-identical.

test_adequacy.note: The three new tests assert real outcomes and would all have failed against the old code, which threw IllegalArgumentException out of PageRequest.of. The parameterized test covers both boundary values, and an ArgumentCaptor pins the Pageable page index at zero rather than settling for status 200, so a clamp applied to only one of the two call sites would still fail. Both routes, plain listing and last-name search, are covered.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved with empty findings lists. The two recommendations are explicitly non-defect and non-blocking: the test reviewer notes a cosmetic overlap between the parameterized test and the status-and-view test, and the security reviewer records that no NVD supply-chain check ran offline against an unchanged dependency baseline this diff does not touch.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, zero design revisions. The diff matches the design-block primary paths exactly, the three test names match the prd-entry verbatim, and the identical unguarded arithmetic in VetController was left alone as the design-block directed rather than widening the slice.

rationale: A one-line boundary clamp in a single controller method, correct at every int including Integer.MIN_VALUE, with tests that fail against the old code and a clean unanimous review. Confirm and merge. Worth a separate slice: VetController.showVetList still carries the same unguarded page arithmetic.
